'''Nagakura Shrine''' (ながくらじんじゃ) is a Shinto shrine located in Nishigō Village, Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima Prefecture. It is a minor shrine listed in the Engishiki, and its former shrine rank was village shrine.

=== Enshrined deities ===
The principal enshrined deity is Izanagi-no-Mikoto, with the Kumano deities enshrined jointly.

=== History ===
The date of foundation is unknown. Since there is a record stating that it was listed as an official shrine in February of the 2nd year of Saikō (855) (in the *Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku*), it is considered to have been founded prior to that time. In the *Engishiki Jinmyōchō*, compiled in the 5th year of Engō (927), it is recorded as “Nagakura Shrine, Shirakawa District, Mutsu Province,” and is listed as a minor shrine.

In the 2nd year of Meiji (1869), the shrine buildings and sacred treasures were destroyed by a mountain fire. In the 5th year of Meiji (1872), the shrine was renamed from Shinmei Shrine back to Nagakura Shrine.

=== Shrine grounds ===
The haiden and honden were rebuilt after the fire of 1869, and in the 9th year of Heisei (1997) they were designated as cultural properties of Nishigō Village.

=== Access ===
* From “Shirakawa Station” on the JR East Tōhoku Main Line: 2 km northwest (about 30 minutes on foot)
* From “Shin-Shirakawa Station” on the JR East Tōhoku Main Line and Tōhoku Shinkansen: 3 km north (about 40 minutes on foot)
